title: Trump Pauses New Russia Sanctions Amid Growing Tensions
subtitle: The decision to block planned economic penalties has sparked a sharp reaction from Ukraine and lawmakers in Washington.

summary.en: President Donald Trump has stopped a new set of sanctions against Russia just days before they were set to begin. The law aimed to punish Russia for its war in Ukraine by targeting its energy sector and financial systems. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized the move as a reward for Vladimir Putin. Many US lawmakers from both parties also expressed strong disagreement with the president's decision. The situation highlights the growing distance between the current US administration and the Ukrainian government.
summary.zh: 川普總統在針對俄羅斯的一系列新制裁措施預定生效前夕，下令將其擱置。該法律旨在透過針對俄國能源與金融體系，懲罰其在烏克蘭發動的戰爭。烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基批評此舉是對普丁的獎賞。許多美國兩黨國會議員也對總統的決定表達強烈不滿。此局勢凸顯了當前美國政府與烏克蘭政府之間日益擴大的距離。

paragraphs.en: President Donald Trump has blocked a series of new sanctions against Russia just two days before they were scheduled to take effect. The sanctions were part of a law passed by the US Congress in September. This law was designed to put heavy pressure on the Russian economy by targeting its energy sector, financial institutions, and a "shadow fleet"—a group of ships used to transport oil while avoiding international rules. The law also gave the president the power to place high taxes, known as tariffs, of up to 100% on countries that buy large amounts of Russian oil and gas.
paragraphs.zh: 川普總統在針對俄羅斯的一系列新制裁措施預定生效的前兩天，下令將其擱置。這些制裁是美國國會於九月通過的一項法律的一部分。該法律旨在透過針對俄國的能源產業、金融機構以及一個被稱為「影子船隊」的組織（即一群用來運輸石油以規避國際規則的船隻），對俄國經濟施加沉重壓力。該法律還賦予總統權力，可對購買大量俄國石油與天然氣的國家徵收高達百分之百的關稅。

paragraphs.en: However, on Friday night, President Trump issued an executive order to pause these measures. He told Congress that stopping the sanctions was in the national interest of the United States. This decision has caused a significant disagreement between the US administration and the government of Ukraine. Relations between Washington and Kyiv have become increasingly difficult recently, especially after the US made a deal to import diesel from Russia. Ukraine has also accused the US of reducing important military support.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，川普總統在週五晚間發布了一項行政命令，暫停了這些措施。他向國會表示，停止制裁符合美國的國家利益。這項決定導致美國政府與烏克蘭政府之間出現了嚴重的分歧。華盛頓與基輔近期的關係日益緊張，特別是在美國達成一項從俄國進口柴油的協議之後。烏克蘭也指責美國削減了重要的軍事援助。

paragraphs.en: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reacted strongly to the news. According to The Guardian, he described the decision as a "reward" for Vladimir Putin and warned that it would encourage the Russian leader to continue his war. Zelenskyy stated that the sanctions could have helped "enormously" to put pressure on Russia. He also noted that the decision came at a time when Russia had launched major attacks on Ukraine’s power plants, attempting to leave cities without electricity before the winter months. Zelenskyy expressed his fear that the US is moving toward better business ties with the Kremlin, which he believes will not stop Putin from continuing his aggression.
paragraphs.zh: 烏克蘭總統澤倫斯基對此消息反應強烈。根據《衛報》報導，他形容這項決定是對普丁的「獎賞」，並警告這將鼓勵這位俄國領導人繼續他的戰爭。澤倫斯基表示，這些制裁本來可以「極大」地幫助對俄國施壓。他也指出，這項決定發布之際，正值俄國對烏克蘭的發電廠發動大規模攻擊，試圖在冬季來臨前讓烏克蘭城市陷入停電。澤倫斯基表達了他的擔憂，認為美國正朝著與克里姆林宮建立更緊密商業關係的方向發展，他相信這無法阻止普丁繼續其侵略行為。

paragraphs.en: In Washington, the president’s move faced a wave of criticism from members of both the Democratic and Republican parties. Many lawmakers argued that the decision ignores the clear intent of Congress, which passed the sanctions law with a very large majority. Only 11 senators had voted against the original legislation. According to the BBC, Congressman Don Beyer accused the president of giving up to Moscow and turning his back on Ukraine. Other Republicans were equally critical. Senator John Cornyn of Texas called the move "reckless," warning that if Putin is not stopped in Ukraine, he might target US allies in NATO next. Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina described the decision as "beyond irresponsible."
paragraphs.zh: 在華盛頓，總統的舉動面臨來自民主黨與共和黨議員的強烈批評。許多國會議員主張，這項決定無視了國會的明確意圖，因為當初這項制裁法案是以壓倒性多數通過的，僅有十一位參議員投下反對票。根據 BBC 報導，眾議員貝爾指責總統向莫斯科屈服，並背棄了烏克蘭。其他共和黨人也同樣嚴厲批評。德州參議員柯寧稱此舉「魯莽」，並警告若不在烏克蘭阻止普丁，他接下來可能會將目標轉向美國在北約的盟友。北卡羅來納州參議員提利斯則形容這項決定「極度不負責任」。

paragraphs.en: Even some of the president’s usual allies expressed their disappointment. Senator Ted Cruz, also from Texas, stated that he wished the president had not taken this action. He suggested that there were other ways to handle energy prices without helping the Russian government. Meanwhile, Representative Don Bacon warned that many lawmakers would now be less likely to support the president’s future plans, as they feel he is supporting a dictator while leaving an ally behind.
paragraphs.zh: 甚至連一些總統平日的盟友也表達了失望。同樣來自德州的參議員克魯茲表示，他希望總統沒有採取這項行動。他建議，還有其他方式可以處理能源價格問題，而不必協助俄國政府。與此同時，眾議員貝肯警告，許多國會議員現在不太可能支持總統未來的計畫，因為他們認為總統在留下盟友的同時，卻在支持一位獨裁者。

paragraphs.en: On the other side, the Russian government welcomed the news. Kirill Dmitriev, a Russian envoy, called the pause an "important and truly historic moment." He claimed that the sanctions would have caused serious damage to the US and global markets, and he argued that economic cooperation between the two nations is beneficial. This view stands in direct contrast to the position held by the Ukrainian government and many US officials who see the sanctions as a necessary tool to end the war.
paragraphs.zh: 另一方面，俄國政府對此消息表示歡迎。俄國特使德米特里耶夫稱這次暫停是一個「重要且真正具有歷史意義的時刻」。他聲稱，這些制裁本會對美國及全球市場造成嚴重損害，並主張兩國之間的經濟合作是有益的。這種觀點與烏克蘭政府及許多美國官員的立場形成直接對比，後者認為制裁是結束戰爭的必要工具。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the sanctions, tensions have also risen over technology. Zelenskyy has reported that Starlink internet terminals, which are used by the Ukrainian military, have been limited. He claimed that these systems stop working when they move at high speeds, which makes it difficult for Ukrainian forces to operate drones. The Ukrainian government believes these restrictions were a deliberate attempt to interfere with their operations, though the US administration has denied limiting access to the network.
paragraphs.zh: 除了制裁之外，科技方面的緊張局勢也隨之升溫。澤倫斯基指出，烏克蘭軍方使用的星鏈網路終端機已受到限制。他聲稱，這些系統在高速移動時會停止運作，導致烏軍難以操作無人機。烏克蘭政府認為這些限制是蓄意干擾其行動的行為，儘管美國政府否認曾限制對該網路的存取。

paragraphs.en: As the situation continues to develop, the future of US-Ukraine relations remains uncertain. Zelenskyy has called for European nations to start their own negotiations with Moscow, as he believes the current US government is no longer a reliable partner in the effort to stop the war. With the sanctions now on hold, the international community is watching closely to see if the US will lift more measures in the future or if pressure from Congress will force a change in policy.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著局勢持續發展，美烏關係的未來仍充滿不確定性。澤倫斯基已呼籲歐洲國家自行與莫斯科展開談判，因為他認為目前的美國政府在阻止戰爭的努力上已不再是可靠的夥伴。隨著制裁目前處於擱置狀態，國際社會正密切關注美國未來是否會解除更多措施，或者國會的壓力是否會迫使政策發生轉變。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop or prevent something from happening or moving forward.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（街區、積木），這裡作動詞用。文中：President Donald Trump has blocked a series of new sanctions against Russia just two days before they were scheduled to take effect.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop trying or to surrender to someone else's demands.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指對某人或某事屈服，而非單純的「放棄」。文中：Congressman Don Beyer accused the president of giving up to Moscow and turning his back on Ukraine.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop supporting or helping someone who previously relied on you.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「轉身背對」，引申為背棄某人。文中：Congressman Don Beyer accused the president of giving up to Moscow and turning his back on Ukraine.

常用於電話等待，這裡指政策被暫時擱置。文中：With the sanctions now on hold, the international community is watching closely to see if the US will lift more measures in the future or if pressure from Congress will force a change in policy.

quiz.question: What specific action did the US Congress take regarding the sanctions before the president blocked them?

options.A: They voted to increase tariffs on Russian energy to 200%.
options.B: They passed a law with a large majority to target the Russian energy sector and shadow fleet.
options.C: They requested an executive order to pause the sanctions for the winter months.
options.D: They held a debate on whether to support the Ukrainian military or the Russian economy.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，國會在九月通過了一項法律，旨在透過針對俄羅斯的能源部門、金融機構及「影子船隊」來施加壓力。選項 A 錯誤，因為文中提到的是最高 100% 的關稅，而非 200%。選項 C 錯誤，因為這項法律是國會通過的，並非國會請求行政命令暫停。選項 D 雖然提到相關議題，但並非該法律的主要內容。

quiz.question: Based on the article, why might the US administration's relationship with Ukraine be deteriorating?

options.A: Because Ukraine refused to accept US-made diesel imports.
options.B: Because the US is angry that Ukraine is negotiating directly with the Kremlin.
options.C: Because the US has been prioritizing its own economic interests over military support for Ukraine.
options.D: Because Ukraine has officially declared the US a non-reliable partner in the UN.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。綜合文章第二段與第三段，美國不僅與俄羅斯達成柴油進口協議，還暫停了對俄制裁，且烏克蘭指控美國減少軍事支持。這顯示美國將自身經濟利益（能源與商業）置於對烏克蘭的軍事承諾之上，導致兩國關係惡化。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 文中未提及；選項 D 雖然澤倫斯基表達了不信任，但並未提到在聯合國正式宣佈。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'reckless' mean as used by Senator John Cornyn?

options.A: Careless and lacking concern for the potential negative consequences.
options.B: Highly calculated and strategic in terms of international diplomacy.
options.C: Physically dangerous and involving direct military combat.
options.D: Technically complex and difficult for the public to understand.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第四段中，參議員 John Cornyn 將總統暫停制裁的行為稱為「reckless」（魯莽的），並警告如果不阻止普丁，他可能會攻擊北約盟友。這顯示該詞意指行動者忽視了潛在的嚴重後果。選項 B 與文意相反；選項 C 過於狹隘，該詞在此指政策決策而非軍事行動；選項 D 則與決策的性質無關。

quiz.question: What is the central theme of this article?

options.A: The technical details of how Russian oil is transported via the 'shadow fleet'.
options.B: The history of the diplomatic relationship between the US and Russia since the war began.
options.C: The internal and international controversy caused by the US president's decision to pause sanctions on Russia.
options.D: The specific military strategies used by Ukraine to defend its power plants from Russian attacks.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。整篇文章圍繞著美國總統暫停對俄制裁這一事件展開，並詳細描述了烏克蘭的強烈反對、美國兩黨議員的批評、俄羅斯的歡迎，以及對美烏關係的影響。選項 A、B、D 皆僅為文章中的部分細節或背景資訊，無法涵蓋全文探討的核心衝突與政治影響。
